rounds.text: Goblin India Ltd trades at an exceptionally deep discount, marked by a price-to-book ratio of just 0.26x against a sector benchmark of 3.77x [E2, E7] and a trailing P/E of 6.79x compared to a sector benchmark of 35.78x [E1, E6]. This extreme valuation disconnect occurs despite robust underlying profit growth, with compounded profit growth reaching 327% over 3 years and 59% over the trailing twelve months [E18, E19]. Fundamentals have aggressively outpaced the stock's performance; five-year profit growth of 23% stands in stark contrast to a negative five-year share price growth of -17%, a divergence where profit growth exceeds one-year price growth by 114% [E17, E20, E53, E54]. Furthermore, the discounted cash flow model calculates an intrinsic value yielding a margin of safety of 83.4%, and a reverse DCF implies the market is irrationally pricing in -7.2% earnings growth when base assumptions require 18.0% [E42, E43, E44]. Operating margins have also expanded by 4 percentage points to 7% in March 2026 compared to three years prior, supported by a broader Consumer Durables sector tailwind score of up to 0.75 [E27, E72, E73]. Conceded: [E4], [E8], [E12], [E22], [E28], [E31], [E38], [E51], [E57], [E58], [E62].

Goblin India Ltd trades at an extremely depressed valuation of 0.26x book value with a share price of ₹ 7.66 against a book value of ₹ 29.9 [E2], alongside a modest P/E ratio of 6.79x [E1] that sits far below the sector benchmark P/E of 35.78x [E6] and sector P/B of 3.77x [E7]. This disconnect between fundamental value and price is further highlighted by a discounted cash flow model yielding an intrinsic value of ₹ 46 per share, providing an overwhelming margin of safety of 83.4% [E42, E43]. Meanwhile, a reverse DCF calculation demonstrates that the current market price incorrectly prices in a negative earnings growth of -7.2%, which stands in stark contrast to the base-case assumption of 18.0% growth [E44]. The underlying business has shown powerful profit momentum over multiple timeframes, achieving a compounded profit growth of 23% over 5 years, 327% over 3 years, and 59% in the trailing twelve months [E17, E18, E19], while operating within a Consumer Durables sector that enjoys a clear macroeconomic tailwind [E72, E73]. Conceded: [E21, E22, E48, E60, E62].
